The test image shows a corn ear with extensive white to grayish-white mold covering kernels in the center of the ear, with some possible greenish tinge. Healthy yellow kernels visible on the sides. This is clearly an ear rot. Key candidates: Ear_rots_Diplodia (white mold), Ear_rots_Trichoderma (dark green), Fusarium (salmon/pink with starburst).

Let me view reference images for the top candidates.

Looking at the references:
- Diplodia: more tan/brown uniform rot across whole ear
- Trichoderma: distinctly dark green — doesn't match
- Fusarium: scattered white mold among yellow kernels with some cottony growth

The test image shows concentrated white-gray cottony mold covering a central band of the ear with some slight greenish tinge. Let me check Gibberella and Aspergillus references.
I need to view more references to meet the minimum requirement. Let me check additional classes.

All leaf/stalk diseases confirmed irrelevant. The test image is clearly an ear rot with dense white-to-grayish-white cottony mold.

**Analysis Summary:**

**Test image features:**
- Dense, white, fluffy/cottony mold covering a large central section of the corn ear
- Slight greenish tinge in portions of the mold
- Healthy yellow kernels visible on both sides of the affected zone
- Mold appears thick, almost foam-like

**Ear rot comparisons:**
- **Ear_rots_Trichoderma**: Dark green — clearly doesn't match
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella**: Pink/red from tip — doesn't match
- **Ear_rots_Aspergillus**: Olive-green powdery mold — the greenish tinge is possible but mold here is more cottony than powdery; typically starts at tip
- **Ear_rots_Diplodia**: White mold (early) becoming grayish-brown, starts at base — reference showed more tan-brown uniform rot over entire ear
- **Fusarium**: White to pinkish cottony mold concentrated in sections of the ear, can appear among healthy kernels — the reference top-right showed white mold concentrated across a band of the ear with yellow kernels on sides, closely matching the test image pattern

The white, dense, cottony mold concentrated in a broad central zone of the ear with healthy kernels on the sides is most consistent with Fusarium ear rot. While classic Fusarium shows pink/salmon coloration, the extensive white mycelial growth concentrated in a section of the ear among healthy kernels matches the Fusarium reference image pattern most closely.
